messages.content:
Forecast date: 2025-04-29. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge and the mathematical target below.

Problem: Hodge conjecture
Mathematical target, paraphrased from the original Clay formulation: For every smooth projective algebraic variety X over the complex numbers and every integer p, determine whether each rational cohomology class in H^(2p)(X,Q) that has Hodge type (p,p) is a rational linear combination of cohomology classes of algebraic cycles of codimension p. The question connects topological information in cohomology with subvarieties defined by algebraic equations. The target is the general rational Hodge conjecture for this class of varieties, with rational coefficients in the combination; an integral-coefficient variant or a statement about arbitrary complex manifolds is a different assertion.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution meeting that mathematical target is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into the solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not meet this event definition.

Assign a probability to the event occurring on or before each of the listed deadlines. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly these five year keys and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's tackle this. The user wants a forecast for the Hodge conjecture solution with AI contribution by certain deadlines up to 2050. Starting from 2025-04-29, the forecast date.

First, the Hodge conjecture is one of the Clay problems, notoriously hard. It's about connecting cohomology classes with algebraic cycles. I know that even partial results are sparse. Most mathematicians haven't solved it yet. AI's role in math is growing, but in what ways? Maybe in generating conjectures, checking cases, or finding unexpected patterns.

The event requires a correct complete solution with an AI-contributed proof step. The AI has to provide a new argument that's part of the solution. The solution must be publicly available and validated by later checks, even if the Clay prize isn't awarded yet.

Now, when could this happen? Let's consider the timelines. AI has been used more in math recently. For example, DeepMind worked with mathematicians on some conjectures. But Hodge is a big leap. The conjecture is deep in algebraic geometry and requires highly abstract reasoning. AI might assist in exploring special cases, but a full proof?

The 2026 deadline is just 1.5 years from now. That's short. Unlikely, maybe 5% chance. By 2030 (5 years), perhaps 15%. AI progress could accelerate, but Hodge is so hard. 2035 (10 years) might be 30%. If AI develops better at handling abstract math, maybe. 2040 (15 years) could be 50%, if breakthroughs in AI and math. 2050 (25 years) maybe 70%, as more time for AI to mature and collaborate effectively. But there's a chance it might never happen, so probabilities shouldn't reach 1.

Need to make sure the probabilities are non-decreasing. Starting low and increasing each deadline. Also, considering that the problem might be too hard even with AI, so never occurs, but the probabilities can't go to 1. Assigning the percentages as such.
